name: Sikadur-42 HP
paste:
SIKADUR®-42 HP: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikadur®-42 HP, April 2023, Version 01.03 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/p/sikadur_-42_hp.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikadur®-42 HP where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.03).
1.2 Product description. Sikadur®-42 HP, is a high strength, multi purpose, three-component, low exotherm, low dusting, solvent-free, moisture-insensitive, epoxy grouting system designed to seat and support high demand equipment.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sikadur®-42 HP may only be used by experienced professionals.
    - Precision seating of baseplates
    - Grouting under equipment, including heavy impact and vibratory machinery, reciprocating engines, compressors, pumps, presses, etc.
    - Grouting under crane rails
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.10.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikadur®-42 HP
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: DEEP POUR PRE-PROPORTIONED, PRECISION EPOXY GROUTING SYSTEM
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (April 2023, Version 01.03) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - ASTM C 1339: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Effective bearing area (p.1).
    - AS 1478.2:2005: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Compressive strength (p.1).
    - ASTM D 695-96: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Modulus of elasticity in compression (p.2).
    - ASTM C 580: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile strength in flexure (p.2).
    - EN 53452: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Modulus of elasticity in flexure (p.2).
    - ASTM D 638: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile strength (p.2).
    - EN 1542: cited with a stated property or value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.2).
    - EN 12188: cited with a stated property or value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.2).
    - ISO 4624: cited with a stated property or value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.2).
    - ASTM C 882: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Shear adhesion strength (p.2).
    - ASTM C 1181: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Creep (p.2).
    - ASTM C 531: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Coefficient of thermal expansion (p.2); Technical Information > Shrinkage (p.2).
    - EN 52450: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Shrinkage (p.2).
    - ASTM C 884: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Thermal compatibility (p.2).
    - ASTM C 413: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Water absorption (p.2).
    - ASTM D 2471: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Application Information > Peak exotherm (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Low peak exotherm.
    - Low dusting, ready-to-mix, pre-proportioned kits.
    - Moisture insensitive.
    - Corrosion and impact resistant.
    - Stress and chemical resistant.
    - High compressive, tensile and shear strengths.
    - High vibration resistance.
    - Low coefficient of thermal expansion, compatible with concrete.
    - Material does not require heated transportation.
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Density: 2,130 kg/m3 (A+B+C)
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Effective bearing area: > 90% (ASTM C 1339)
    - Modulus of elasticity in compression: ~ 18,000 MPa (ASTM D 695-96)
    - Tensile strength in flexure: > 35 MPa (ASTM C 580)
    - Modulus of elasticity in flexure: ~ 16,000 MPa (EN 53452)
    - Tensile strength: > 14 MPa (ASTM D 638)
    - Tensile strain at break: 0.1 ± 0.05% (7 days at +23°C) (ISO 75)
    - Shear adhesion strength: > 47 MPa (concrete failure) (ASTM C 882)
    - Creep: 4.14 N/mm2 / 31’500 N (+60°C) 1.10%; 2.76 N/mm2 / 21’000 N (+60°C) 0.21%; API requirements: 0.5% with 2.76 N/mm2 load (ASTM C 1181)
    - Shrinkage: Linear Shrinkage: -0.027%; Linear Shrinkage: -0.03% (ASTM C 531) (EN 52450)
    - Coefficient of thermal expansion: 2.1 x 10⁻⁵ mm/mm/°C (Temp. range -30°C to +30°C); 4.4 x 10⁻⁵ mm/mm/°C (Temp. range +24°C to +100°C) (ASTM C 531)
    - Thermal compatibility: No delamination / pass (ASTM C 884)
    - Water absorption: 0.059% (7 days) (ASTM C 413)
2.7 Compressive strength.
    | 6 hrs | ~ 20 MPa |
    | 1 day | ~ 90 MPa |
    | 7 days | ~ 100 MPa |
    Test method printed: (AS 1478.2:2005)
    Note printed: Test specimen cured and tested at +23 oC and 50 mm cube size.
2.8 Tensile adhesion strength.
    | ~ 9 MPa (on steel) | (ISO 4624, EN 1542 and EN 12188) |
    | > 3.5 MPa (concrete failure) |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
2.9 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 36 kg - 3 component kit consisting of: 472516 Sikadur 42 HP Part A - Resin 5 kg; 472519 Sikadur 42 HP Part B - Hardener 1 kg; 731898 Sikadur 42 HP Part C 15 kg bag (2 x 15 kg Bags per kit)
    - Shelf life: 24 months from date of production
    - Storage conditions: Stored properly in original and unopened, sealed and undamaged packaging, in dry conditions at temperatures between +5°C and +30°C. Protect from direct sun light.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.03) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality.
    - Mortar and concrete must be older than 28 days (dependent on minimum strength requirements).
    - Verify the substrate strength (concrete, natural stone etc.).
    - The substrate surface (all types) must be clean, dry and free from contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, existing surface treatments and coatings etc.
    - Steel substrates must be de-rusted to a standard equivalent to Sa 2.5.
    - The substrate must be sound and all loose particles must be removed.
    - Substrate must be dry or mat damp and free from any standing water, ice etc.
3.3 Substrate preparation. Surface and base plate contact area must be clean and sound. For best results, the substrate should be dry. Remove dust, laitance, oils, grease, curing compounds, impregnations, waxes, foreign particles, coatings, and disintegrated materials by mechanical means, i.e. chipping with a chisel, blastcleaning etc. All anchor pockets or sleeves must be free of water. Blastcleaning metal base plates to an acceptable quality standard equivalent to SA 2.5 for maximum adhesion. Apply grout immediately to prevent re-oxidizing.
3.4 Substrate preparation - Forming. The consistency of the Sikadur®-42 HP epoxy grout system requires the use of permanent or temporary forms to contain the material around base plates, for example. In order to prevent leakage or seepage, all of these formers must be sealed. Apply polyethylene film or wax to all forms to prevent adhesion of the grout. Prepare the formwork to maintain more than 100 mm liquid head to facilitate placement. A grout box equipped with an inclined trough attached to the form will enhance the grout flow and minimize air encapsulation.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.03) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Yield: 36 kg kit yields approximately 16.9 litres of grout
    - Peak exotherm: 44°C (at +23°C) (ASTM D 2471)
4.3 Mixing ratio. Part A : B : C = 1.67 : 0.33 : 10 by weight (Standard); Solid / liquid = 5 : 1 by weight; Possibility to adjust the Mixing ratio, depending on Flowability: Part A : B : C = 1.67 : 0.33 : (9-12) by weight; Solid / liquid = (4.5 – 6) : 1 by weight
4.4 Layer thickness. Minimum grout depth: 10 mm; Maximum grout depth: 150 mm
    | Temperature | Layer thickness maximum |
    | 10 oC - 20 oC | 150 mm |
    | 20 oC - 30 oC | 120 mm |
4.5 Pot Life. (200g, adiabatic testing)
    | 5 : 1 : 30 | 130 mins at +10 oC | 75-80 mins at +23 oC |
    The potlife begins when the resin and hardener are mixed. It is shorter at high temperatures and longer at low temperatures. The greater the quantity mixed, the shorter the potlife. To obtain longer workability at high temperatures, the mixed adhesive may be divided into portions. Another method is to chill parts A+B and C before mixing them (i.e. only when application temperatures are above +20°C).
4.6 Mixing - Pre-batched units.
    - Mix components A and B in the component A pail for 3 min with a paddle attached to a low speed drill (300- 450 rpm). Avoid aeration while mixing until the material becomes uniformly blended in colour and viscosity. Place the mixed epoxy into an appropriate mixing vessel. Slowly add the contents of component C (to keep air entrapment at a minimum) dependent on flow requirements (observe the correct mixing ratio) and mix until uniform and homogeneous. (approx. 5 min)
    - Mix only that quantity which can be used within its potlife.
4.7 Mixing - Bulk packing (not pre-batched).
    - First, stir each component thoroughly. Add the components in the correct proportions into a suitable mixing pail. Mix the components. Use an electric low speed mixer, etc as above for the pre-batched units. Never mix Component A and B without adding component C (as the exothermic reaction between A and B alone generates excess heat)
    - Leave Sikadur®-42 HP to stand in the normal mixing vessel until the majority of entrained air bubbles have dispersed.
4.8 Application method / tools.
    - Pour the mixed grout into the prepared forms from one or two sides only, to eliminate air entrapment. Maintain the liquid head to ensure intimate contact to the base plate. Place sufficient epoxy grout in the forms to rise slightly above the underside (3 mm) of the base plate. The minimum void depth beneath the base-plate shall be 12 mm. Where the void beneath the base plate is greater than 150 mm, place the epoxy grout in successive 150 mm lifts or less, once the preceding lift has cooled.
    - Once hardened check the adhesion by tapping with a hammer.
4.9 Cleaning of equipment. Sweep excess grout into appropriate containers for disposal before it has hardened. Dispose of in accordance with applicable local regulations. Uncured material can be removed with Sika Colma Cleaner. Cured material can only be removed mechanically.
4.10 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Minimum substrate temperature: +10°C. The material must be conditioned by being stored in an area with an ambient temperature between +10°and +30°C for a minimum of 48 h before using. Do not thin with solvents. Solvents will prevent proper curing and change mechanical properties.
    - Sikadur®-42 HP is a vapour barrier when cured. Minimum grout depth: 10 mm. Maximum grout depth: 150 mm per lift. The last lift must be kept at 50 mm. Component C must be kept dry. For specific bolt grouting applications please refer to Sika Technical Services. For proper seating, allow the grout to rise above the bottom (3 mm) of the base plate.
    - Avoid splitting prebatched units to mix. Mix complete units only. Cold ambient, substrate or material temperatures will influence the curing and flow characteristics of Sikadur®-42 HP. Do not subject cured epoxy grout to sudden temperature changes especially during early curing stages. Contact Sika Technical Services for control joint spacing on large base plate grouting projects.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Material temperature. Sikadur®-42 HP must be applied at temperatures between +10°C and +30°C. Condition the material by also storing at this temperature for 48 hours before use.
5.3 Ambient air temperature. +10°C min. / +30°C max.
5.4 Substrate temperature. +10°C min. / +30°C max.
5.5 Substrate moisture content. ≤ 4% pbw
5.6 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.10):
    - Minimum substrate temperature: +10°C. The material must be conditioned by being stored in an area with an ambient temperature between +10°and +30°C for a minimum of 48 h before using. Do not thin with solvents. Solvents will prevent proper curing and change mechanical properties.
    - Avoid splitting prebatched units to mix. Mix complete units only. Cold ambient, substrate or material temperatures will influence the curing and flow characteristics of Sikadur®-42 HP. Do not subject cured epoxy grout to sudden temperature changes especially during early curing stages. Contact Sika Technical Services for control joint spacing on large base plate grouting projects.
5.7 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Effective bearing area: > 90% (ASTM C 1339)
    - Compressive strength: 6 hrs | ~ 20 MPa; 1 day | ~ 90 MPa; 7 days | ~ 100 MPa (AS 1478.2:2005)
    - Modulus of elasticity in compression: ~ 18,000 MPa (ASTM D 695-96)
    - Tensile strength in flexure: > 35 MPa (ASTM C 580)
    - Modulus of elasticity in flexure: ~ 16,000 MPa (EN 53452)
    - Tensile strength: > 14 MPa (ASTM D 638)
    - Tensile strain at break: 0.1 ± 0.05% (7 days at +23°C) (ISO 75)
    - Shear adhesion strength: > 47 MPa (concrete failure) (ASTM C 882)
    - Creep: 4.14 N/mm2 / 31’500 N (+60°C) 1.10%; 2.76 N/mm2 / 21’000 N (+60°C) 0.21%; API requirements: 0.5% with 2.76 N/mm2 load (ASTM C 1181)
    - Shrinkage: Linear Shrinkage: -0.027%; Linear Shrinkage: -0.03% (ASTM C 531) (EN 52450)
    - Coefficient of thermal expansion: 2.1 x 10⁻⁵ mm/mm/°C (Temp. range -30°C to +30°C); 4.4 x 10⁻⁵ mm/mm/°C (Temp. range +24°C to +100°C) (ASTM C 531)
    - Thermal compatibility: No delamination / pass (ASTM C 884)
    - Water absorption: 0.059% (7 days) (ASTM C 413)
    - Peak exotherm: 44°C (at +23°C) (ASTM D 2471)
5.8 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.9 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikadur®-42 HP, April 2023, Version 01.03, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/p/sikadur_-42_hp.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikadur®-42 HP Part A, version 13/07/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/l/sds-sikadur-42-hpparta.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikadur®-42 HP Part B, version 18/06/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/e/sds-sikadur-42-hppartb.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikadur®-42 HP Part C, version 02/07/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/x/sds-sikadur-42-hppartc.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Sikadur 42HP Part B, version 07/11/2022, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/b/Sikadur%2042HP%20Part%20B.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
